about: Facts about trails from resort and club pages, beyond OpenStreetMap. Descriptions are short summaries in our own words, each linked to its source. n: names (OpenStreetMap spellings first), matched within r metres of c. no: number on the official map, kind: the source's trail type, where: part of the mountain, km: the source's length.

trails.text: Double-track road; part of the multi-use network.
Wide fire road with gentle grades through cedar forest and good views. Made for riders who are new to riding off pavement.
Gravel road back to the base, much like Boom Trail.
Fire road used to get to the Provincial Park.
Starts as a wide gravel fire road and turns into wide trail with small berms, rollers and gentle grades through the trees.
One of Fernie's first downhill trails: fast, fall-line and technical through the forest. Racers love it.
Like Will Power, with more rock and loose soil.
Technical corners, several line choices and a few drops and jumps.
Steep pitches into supported corners, with off-camber roots.
Gentle and smooth, with twists, rollers and bridges through cedar forest. Good for families and kids.
Fast, steep and loose. Committing; experts only.
Fire road through Cedar Bowl to the Provincial Park. Expect long climbs to get back to the base.
Hand-built, winding trail through cedar forest beside Mr. Berms. Good for green riders practising berms and carrying speed.
Singletrack with some wooden features; a harder version of Hollow Tree.
Cross-country trail across the lower mountain through shady forest, with bridges over creeks.
Small berms and easy traverses up top. Halfway down you can go to Deer Trail, or carry on to the lower part with bigger berms, which leads to Honey Bee and Eville.
New in 2026: a blue jump trail for progressing, through shady forest and over a creek, ending at Holo Bike and Eville.
Black flow trail with big berms and advanced features. You need to be able to jump.
Short, playful jump trail into the base.
Classic steep singletrack down a cedar ravine, with steeps and drops and a flowy finish.
Medium difficulty, with natural roots, rocks and rollers.
Next to Phat Larry's, but with easier grades.
Home to the resort's biggest built wooden features.
Singletrack side route running alongside Cedar Trail.

Technical corners, off-camber roots and rocky sections, with valley views halfway down. A short top section (from Trespass Trail to Diamond Back) is double black for its must-do drops and rooty corners; the rest is black.
Technical but flowy descent with plenty of natural features.
Old-school downhill trail with rock rolls, tight corners and forest sections. Below Rock Landing the lower part adds technical features and jumps.
Fresh hand-built line in the forest, reached from Lower Rumplestumpskin.
Fire road across the mountain's bowls with big views and a lot of pedalling. Rated black.
Drops in from Diamond Back corner and takes a fast, direct line through steep old-growth cedars.
A favourite: fast, flowy berms and jumps. Every feature can be rolled, so it suits mixed-ability groups or riders stepping up.
Machine-built, fast way to get to Top Gun.
Warm-up trail across a ski run with berms and rollers. A good first blue trail.
Like Eville but bigger: fast, flowy berms and jumps.
Green flow trail through open forest back to the Holo Bike connector, with small jumps and berms to build confidence.
Tight trail through the forest with low ladders and bridges that test balance.
Technically demanding trail through shady forest, with some natural drops and roots.
A rebuild of the lowest part of TNT: machine-built jumps and rollers for progressing on flow and jump trails.
Short technical section that ends on a long wooden ramp down to the parking lot.
On the Kodiak run and as steep and technical as Kodiak Karnage: long steep, rooty chutes.
Flowy jump trail through big cedars near the base. Good for ending the day and working on jumps and berms.
Mellow, obstacle-free beginner trail with small berms, for learning to corner and getting used to gravity riding.
A downhill pump track: machine-built berms, rollers and table tops, rideable fast or slow, and good for learning to get air.
Carries on from Dirt Wave: pump the rollers to keep your speed.
High-speed flow trail with table tops and mogul-like rollers.
Intermediate jumps: a place to learn to jump or go bigger.
Park favourite with rollers, gaps and berms all the way down, plus options for bigger features.
Hand-built downhill track: a fast chute in, then a rough, rocky descent with loam and roots.
Steeper, faster flow trail with tight berms top to bottom.
The park's classic loam trail: several hand-built lines through natural features.
A faster, bigger Hot Lap on sandy dirt, with natural doubles and rollers.
Steep, fast loam trail with optional doubles, step-downs and a rock roll.
Hand-built, rooty singletrack with moderate drops and doubles.
Advanced jump trail with rollable table tops, gaps and optional side hits.
Relaxed jump trail that starts with a drop and ramp, then small gaps and steep berms: a step up for jumps and drops.
Starts with a wooden drop, optional doubles all the way, and a wooden gap at the end. Drops and gaps are mandatory.
Very fast, very big gap jumps (40 to 50 ft). Every feature is mandatory.
Jump trail with large gaps, built by the Coastal Crew. Every feature is mandatory.
Uphill only. One of two trails where riding up is allowed in the bike park.
The resort's starting trail: take the gondola to mid-station and ride it back to the village until you're comfortable.
Riding up is also allowed here (Big Easy Climb).

rev.Freeride: Revelstoke's freeride trails are machine-built and need jumping skills: wider, smoother tread with berms, rollers, jumps and wallrides that get bigger with the grade.
rev.Technical: Revelstoke's technical trails are rougher singletrack with roots, rocks and tighter corners; harder grades add steeps and drops.
